craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as light unobjectifiable; vyabhicāri wonder at over-pervasion (C1 rasa block). Sanskrit-first: arkendudīpādi…bhinnam (distinct FROM lit-things — bhinnam governs the catalogue); na ābhāti ativyāptatayā (does NOT shine, BY-over-pervasion — pervasion is WHY, instrumental named); vyavahāra eva (mere convention — eva restricts). Abhinavagupta frame: subject-object vocabulary demoted exactly where the Sanskrit demotes it (deixis row 11: no pointing added). Rows: 9 (sun/moon/lamp bare catalogue — three lights named, none adorned), 1 (‘name’ end-weighted — the convention-word lands last), 10 (no image imported; the verse has none). Bank: Ingalls-fidelity (no new metaphor; music in the joints: colon + dash). Close: ‘a mere transacting name’. Rupture: ‘Hence:’ (denial turns to naming). Rejected: ‘too pervasive to appear’ — killed: essence-words smuggled into song; ‘lamplight’ — killed: new morpheme; ‘Hence:’ on its own line — killed: colon already stages the turn. Read aloud: un-LIKE the LIGHT of SUN, MOON, LAMP — it does NOT shine … OF-light-NA-ture it-SELF — a MERE trans-ACT-ing NAME.

lines: Unlike the light of sun, moon, lamp — it does not shine, pervading too completely. Hence:
of light-nature itself — ‘His illumined-and-illuminator’ is a mere transacting name.
l4.sanskrit_cite: arkendudīpādyavabhāsabhinnaṃ nābhātyativyāptatayā tataśca | prakāśarūpaṃ tadiyatprakāśyaprakāśatākhyā vyavahāra eva

reads_against.argmap: Distinct from every lit thing, light itself does not shine as an object — too pervasive to appear; illumined-vs-illuminator is mere convention. → Light unobjectifiable; subject-object vocabulary demoted.
